note: Plenty of mineral N left by the previous crop gives a denser early canopy, which favours eyespot build-up in cereals. Eyespot incidence rose 2-3 fold at 160 lb N/acre vs no N in a winter-wheat study (Smiley 1996, WSU).
Compacted, poorly drained soil favours Aphanomyces root rot, so the same inoculum costs more yield.
Acid soil weakens nodulation, so legumes leave less nitrogen behind.

Raising pH from 5.2-5.5 to 7.2 reduced clubroot severity by 34-36% and increased canola seed yield by 70-98% (Hwang et al. 2022). Severity alone implies about 1.5x; 2.5x reflects the yield gain. Review if clubroot losses look too large.
Fusarium wilt of legumes is suppressed by alkaline soils and nitrate nutrition (Smiley, WSU review). No Central European effect size found, so a conservative 1.4x below pH 6.

A systematic review of 1771 observations found N fertilisation raised the Fusarium isolate percentage by 61.6% (lnRR 0.48); severity and DON responses were context-dependent. Multiplier 1 + 0.616 x trigger, rounded to 1.6.

In potato, high nematode density and compaction each cut tuber yield by about 27% and the effects were additive (Schans 1995). Nematode-only loss 27% + compaction 27% x (1 - 0.27) = about 46.7%, so about 1.4x at severe compaction.

Compaction reduces drainage and aeration and is reported to aggravate root diseases; the review gives the direction, not a Rhizoctonia-specific size, so a conservative 1.3x at severe compaction. Applies to root crops only (potato, sugar beet).
Dense, poorly aerated soils are reported to be more susceptible to Fusarium and other fungal root diseases (SARE); direction only, so the loss multiplier is limited to 1.3.
Volunteer oilseed rape can carry Plasmodiophora brassicae resting spores between crops (green bridge). Direction established, size not, so +30% clubroot load at high volunteer density.

Mineral N suppresses nodulation and N fixation, so a legume leaves less net N when the soil already holds plenty. Inhibition not quantified in the cited work; conservative 40% cut above 120 kg residual N/ha.

Take-all is more severe in alkaline than acid soil and greatly reduced when rhizosphere pH is below 6.6 (Smiley, WSU). The review gives the threshold, not a yield-loss ratio, so a conservative 1.4x above pH 7.2.
